idiom_name: Semaphore from async-mutex with runExclusive / acquire
implementation_notes: TypeScript types the same promise-based realizations rather than adding a runtime: async-mutex's Semaphore is the explicit class - new Semaphore(initialValue), acquire() resolving to [value, release], runExclusive(weight?, priority?), setValue, cancel() rejecting pending waiters with E_CANCELED - and p-limit is the typed limiter function when a whole-task bound is enough. runExclusive is the release-on-every-exit-path form (it releases when the returned promise settles, including rejection); manual acquire() hands back a release function that must be called in a finally block. Weights and priorities are the reason to choose the class over a limiter.
pitfalls: Manual acquire() gives back a release function that is easy to drop on an early return; prefer runExclusive or wrap the body in try/finally.
A limiter or semaphore duplicated by bundling (two copies of the package in one process) yields two counters for one resource; keep it in a single module and export it.
Atomics.wait throws on the main thread, so a SharedArrayBuffer semaphore must live inside a worker and be typed as Int32Array over SharedArrayBuffer.

variants.name: Blocking semaphore over SharedArrayBuffer (worker_threads)
variants.idiom_name: Int32Array over SharedArrayBuffer with Atomics.wait / Atomics.notify
variants.implementation_notes: When TypeScript runs in worker_threads, a genuinely blocking semaphore is possible: an Int32Array backed by a SharedArrayBuffer holds the permit count, acquisition loops on Atomics.compareExchange and parks with Atomics.wait, release uses Atomics.add plus Atomics.notify, and the main thread must use Atomics.waitAsync or promise-based limiters because Atomics.wait throws there. This is the typed equivalent of a real semaphore and the only form with a blocking acquire in the JavaScript platform.
pitfalls: Typing SharedArrayBuffer requires the ES2017 lib (and cross-origin isolation in browsers), so the tsconfig target/lib must be set deliberately.
Atomics.wait cannot be called on the main thread; the type system will not stop it, so the constraint has to be enforced by module layout.
A compare-exchange loop can spin between wakeups under contention; pair it with Atomics.wait rather than a busy retry.
